messages:
sam (eng-runtime): quick heads-up — after the kv-paging rewrite I ran a precision sweep (fp16/bf16/int8) on longctx workstreams. int8+paging shows ~2.3% PPL regression vs fp16 when context > 16k. can anyone else reproduce?

jordan (eng-runtime): repro here. same setup as staging: dedicated-reserved 8xA100, batch mix of 1/4/8, longctx episodes. int8+paging triggers more compaction and I see huge memcpy spikes in page-mgr.

mira (eng-ml): can you paste the profile? curious if kernel selection is switching to a slower path because of memory layout changes.

sam (eng-runtime): pasting a trimmed perf output — note the page-mgr and generic gemm lines:

```
# perf top sample
page_manager_handle_eviction  47.2%
memcpy                      12.6%
matmul_kernel_generic       20.1%
matmul_kernel_opt_v1        5.3%
kv_slot_lookup              8.4%
```

jordan (eng-runtime): interesting — that matmul_kernel_generic share jumps when page compaction increases fragmentation (more non-contiguous KV). kernel selector falls back because tile shape mispredicts.

lee (eng-infra): infra telemetry shows ~3x increase in minor page faults when the eviction threshold hits 64k slots. paging to CPU pages is much more frequent with int8 due to tighter packing -> more compaction churn.

perf-bot: perf-regression-alert: job/longctx-sweep/1813459 flagged increased p99 latency and lower throughput for int8+paging variant.

mira (eng-ml): hypothesis: dequantization noise compounded by reordering from compaction + fallback kernel numerical differences. propose experiments:
- per-layer precision map (keep K/V in bf16, rest int8)
- bump kv_hot_threshold to reduce churn
- force kernel selection to prefer opt_v1 despite non-contiguous layout (bench for correctness)

sam (eng-runtime): trying per-layer map now — config snippet:
```
kv_precision_map:
  attention.k: bf16
  attention.v: bf16
  feedforward: int8
kv_hot_threshold: 2.0        # multiplier for considering slot hot
compaction_window: 120s
```

jordan (eng-runtime): ran quick run with that config on the repro suite. results:
- int8 baseline (with paging): +2.3% PPL
- bf16 K/V + int8 rest: +0.4% PPL, memory overhead +6.8%
- throughput: bf16-KV down ~8% vs int8 baseline

mira (eng-ml): that looks promising — big win for quality with modest mem/latency tradeoff. we should also check whether switching kernels reproduces the PPL gap by itself: run int8 with forced opt_v1 kernel even on fragmented layout.

lee (eng-infra): ops suggestion: implement a generational eviction policy for kv slots — keep recently accessed slots in a small hot set pinned to GPU memory. should cut compaction frequency. also we can increase the slab size so compaction happens less often (bench cost).

sam (eng-runtime): opened PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/kv-pager/pulls/1427 
- adds per-layer precision map config
- exposes kv_hot_threshold + compaction_window tunables
- adds telemetry counters for page faults vs compaction events

jordan (eng-runtime): +1 to landing after perf tests. but we should revert the earlier tight-packing commit (4f3a8b) if we see continued regressions in the nightly. that commit reduced peak mem by 9% but increased fragmentation.

mira (eng-ml): agree. next steps:
- run kernel-forcing experiment to isolate numeric vs layout causes
- run long 48h stability with per-layer bf16-KV config on staging
- collect token-level evals to measure subtle decodes (not just PPL)

lee (eng-infra): I'll schedule a infra job to reserve a node pool with no preemption so we can run the long stability test.

sam (eng-runtime): thanks. tagging @mira for eval harness and @lee for infra. I'll keep the thread updated with numbers. please react with :thumbsup: if you want me to proceed to a canary rollout for dedicated customers once tests pass.

jordan (eng-runtime): :thumbsup:

mira (eng-ml): :eyes:

sam (eng-runtime): closing loop — initial canary plan if stable: bf16-KV default for longctx jobs + int8 rest, kv_hot_threshold=2.0, compaction_window=120s. will iterate based on telemetry.
